newsitem.title: FRANCE: French grain markets firmer after EU wheat award.
newsitem.headline: French grain markets firmer after EU wheat award.

text.p: French old and new crop wheat prices rose on Friday after the European Union cleared the export of nearly 500,000 tonnes of wheat at Thursday's weekly auction, dealers said.
Maize rose with wheat but barley business was non-existent, they said.
Firm wheat prices turned grain cooperatives into sellers but availability was low as farmers keep a lid on supplies in anticipation of higher prices, dealers added.
On Thursday the EU granted licences for the export of 480,000 tonnes of soft wheat with a refund of 9.30 Ecus per tonne.
Dealers said the volume granted was positive and in line with the pace of recent EU wheat awards as there would be a break in tenders next Thursday for the Easter holiday.
Rouen standard quality wheat for April traded at 895 francs per tonne, up five francs from Thursday, while May delivery for high quality wheat traded at 900 francs.
Standard quality wheat for September-December delivery traded at 875, up 2.50 from Thursday.
Maize into Bordeaux for March-April delivery was bid at 860-865 francs against 855-860 on Thursday, but sellers sought 870.
MATIF fob barge wheat futures for May were trading at 930 francs per tonne, up three francs on Monday. Total trade was 105 lots at 1520 GMT.
